key_insight: A physics-aligned simulator (SIM1) can act as a zero-shot data scaler for deformable-object manipulation by generating realistic, transferable interactions of shape, contact, and topology without relying on real-world labeled data.
problem_solved: Reduces the data bottleneck and sim-to-real mismatch in learning robotic manipulation of deformable objects (cloth, ropes, soft bodies) where traditional rigid-body-focused simulators produce unrealistic dynamics and poor transfer.
method: Design a physics-aligned simulator that explicitly models co-evolving shape, contact, and topology to better reflect deformable dynamics.
Use the simulator as a zero-shot data generator to scale diverse interaction trajectories and motion primitives for training agents without additional real-world labels.
Align simulation priors and procedural variation to maximize out-of-the-box transferability to real deformable manipulation tasks.
impact: Enables practitioners to massively expand training datasets for deformable-object learning with reduced real-world collection cost and improved out-of-the-box transfer, accelerating development of robust cloth and soft-body manipulation systems.
visual_elements: Side-by-side comparison: rigid-body simulator vs SIM1 visualizations showing realistic cloth/soft-body deformation over time
Pipeline diagram: SIM1 -> large-scale synthetic dataset -> zero-shot-trained policy -> real-world deployment
Performance sketch: qualitative transfer examples (grasping/folding cloth) and a schematic bar chart showing improved transferability (sim-to-real) vs baseline simulators
Icon set: cloth/rope/soft-body, physics engine, dataset stack, robot gripper
paper_title: SIM1: Physics-Aligned Simulator as Zero-Shot Data Scaler in Deformable Worlds
paper_authors: Yunsong Zhou, Hangxu Liu, Xuekun Jiang, Xing Shen, Yuanzhen Zhou
